title: Distributable score processor runtime image
description:
Purpose: make the reusable score processor runtime build definition a versioned part of the Plexus Python distribution so consumers can build and validate an image from the same immutable Plexus revision they deploy.

Definition of Done:
- The Lambda handler is importable from the installed Plexus package.
- A self-contained container build definition is shipped in wheel and sdist artifacts.
- Builds require an explicit immutable Plexus source revision and do not depend on a Plexus repository checkout.
- Existing first-party score processor image builds remain functional.
- Reusable repository infrastructure can provision independently named runtime repositories.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Scope correction: the currently deployed score processor is a strict compatibility boundary. The new distributable runtime will be implemented in a separate package/resource tree with its own handler and Dockerfile. Existing score-processor-lambda source, image pipeline, handler entry point, and production behavior will not be modified. Intentional duplication is accepted for parallel-cutover isolation; legacy removal is explicitly out of scope.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Implemented the isolated runtime under plexus/runtime/async_score_processor with a separately packaged handler and Dockerfile. The Dockerfile rejects non-SHA refs, fetches one detached commit using ephemeral GitHub App authentication, installs scoring dependencies from that commit’s poetry.lock, builds and installs the package wheel, and records the source revision. Added a separate configurable repository stack; the legacy score-processor-lambda tree has no diff. Targeted runtime, infrastructure, packaging, and legacy handler tests pass. The local all-tests environment lacks optional all-extra dependencies and contains ignored generated dashboard artifacts, so clean GitHub CI remains the authoritative broad gate.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Removed the new reusable async stack’s mutable image-source reference contract. Consumers now supply only a digest-pinned image URI; the existing independent artifact pipeline remains unchanged for legacy consumers.
